REQ-013.rationale: Art. 6(1) has no lettered points. Art. 8(1) is the classification duty: 'identify, classify and adequately document all ICT supported business functions ... and ICT assets'.

REQ-016.rationale: Art. 7 has no numbered paragraphs. Art. 8(2) is the continuous risk-identification duty: 'identify all sources of ICT risk ... assess cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities'.

REQ-022.rationale: Art. 15 binds the ESAs, not entities. Art. 9(3)(c) requires solutions that 'prevent ... the impairment of the authenticity and integrity' of data; image signing is an authenticity control.

REQ-023b.rationale: Art. 15 binds the ESAs, not entities. Restricting image sources is an authenticity and integrity control under Art. 9(3)(c).

REQ-012.rationale: Art. 5(2)(a) is the management body's ultimate responsibility for ICT risk. Art. 8(6) is the literal inventory duty: 'financial entities shall maintain relevant inventories'.

REQ-025.rationale: Art. 5(2)(d) is the resilience strategy. Art. 8(1) requires entities to 'adequately document all ICT supported business functions ... and ICT assets'.

REQ-027.rationale: Art. 6(2) concerns the framework's contents. Art. 8(4) requires entities to 'map the configuration ... and the links and interdependencies between the different information assets and ICT assets'.

REQ-008.rationale: Art. 9(3)(a) concerns security of data transfer. Art. 9(4)(b) is the network provision: infrastructure must be designed so it can be 'instantaneously severed or segmented'.

REQ-028.rationale: Art. 9(3)(b) concerns data corruption risk. Art. 9(4)(b) covers isolation of information assets; compute segregation sits with it.

REQ-010.rationale: Art. 9(4)(a) is the duty to document an information security policy. Art. 9(4)(c) limits access 'to what is required for legitimate and approved functions and activities only'.

REQ-011.rationale: As REQ-010: 9(4)(a) is a documentation duty; host isolation restricts privilege under 9(4)(c).

REQ-018.rationale: As REQ-010: filesystem and capability hardening restricts privilege under 9(4)(c), not the policy-documentation duty in 9(4)(a).

REQ-003.rationale: Art. 9(4)(b) is network segmentation. Art. 9(4)(c) is the least-privilege provision and expressly addresses 'access rights and ... a sound administration thereof'.

REQ-004.rationale: As REQ-003: RBAC privilege escalation is an access-rights control under 9(4)(c).

REQ-026.rationale: Art. 9(4)(c) governs access limitation. Art. 9(4)(d) is the authentication provision: 'policies and protocols for strong authentication mechanisms'.

REQ-006.rationale: Art. 11(1) establishes the business continuity policy. Art. 11(2)(a) is the operative duty to 'ensure the continuity of the financial entity's critical or important functions'; resource governance prevents contention that breaks continuity.

REQ-007.rationale: Art. 11(1) establishes the policy. Art. 11(5) requires ICT assets be used 'with regard to adequately ensuring the redundancy of all critical components'; minimum replicas is redundancy.

REQ-021.rationale: Art. 11(3) concerns response and recovery plans. Art. 11(6)(a) is the testing duty: 'test the ICT business continuity plans and the ICT response and recovery plans ... at least yearly'.

REQ-015.rationale: Art. 13(1) concerns gathering information on vulnerabilities and threats. Art. 9(4)(e) is expressly ICT change management: changes 'recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner'.
